Madam President, distinguished delegates. I have the honor to present the report of the Fifth Committee. During the main part of the 80th session, the Fifth Committee met from October 6th to December 30th, 2025, holding 20 plenary meetings and numerous informal consultations. A number of the committee's reports were already considered by the General Assembly at its 18th, 42nd, and 69th plenary meetings, and the additional reports of the Fifth Committee containing recommendations for consideration during the main part of the 80th session of the General Assembly are reflected in A/C5/80/INF/3. The General Assembly has not decided on the concept of the responsibility to protect, its scope, implications, and possible forms of implementation, noting that the estimates of thematic cluster 1 comprise narratives, functions, strategy, and external factors, results, performance measures, derivables, or other information related to the Special Adviser to the Secretary-General on the Responsibility to Protect; decides to delete the narratives, functions, strategy, and external factors, results, performance measures, derivables, and other information related to the Special Adviser to the Secretary-General on the responsibility to protect as contained in the strategic framework and related narrative of the Office of the Special Adviser to the Secretary-General on the Prevention of Genocide. Thank you, Madam President. We understand that the proposal to abolish the ASG position in Geneva, as recommended by the ACIBQ, aims to achieve cost efficiency through the reduction of senior-level posts. However, we considered it essential to maintain the ASG-level representation for UN representative to the Geneva international discussions to ensure the effective delivery of the mandate entrusted to this mission. Given the existing workload of the ASGs based in New York, we remain worried that allocating these functions from Geneva to New York-based ASG could negatively affect the effective execution of the UN Representative to the Geneva International Discussions mandate. In this context, we always supported retaining the ASG position in Geneva that is solely dedicated to the GID. We would like to use this occasion to underline again our appreciation for the language introduced by the like-minded group during negotiations. Which sought to preserve the ESG level of the UN representation. The Secretary-General's proposal does not explicitly clarify that the duties of the UNRGID would be assumed by an ESG based in New York. Rather, it refers to a senior-level DPPA/DPO official, which could imply either an ESG or lower-level positions. This ambiguity raises concerns regarding the continuity and authority required for effective mandate implementation. The Georgian delegation notes with regret that above-mentioned certain language on preserving the ESG level of UN representation in the Geneva international discussions, which we considered of utmost importance, was not retained in the final version of the resolution. However, having a strong expectation that the ESG will continue to represent the United Nations in the Geneva international discussions, and in the spirit of maintaining consensus, we will not call for a vote. Having said this, for the record, the delegation of Georgia wishes to place on record its disassociation exclusively with the absence of the language on preserving the ESG level of the UN representation in the Geneva international discussions. Thank you.
